headline: Yesterday's credit truce lasted exactly one session: VIX 34, HY back out 9bp and the megacaps finally cracked — semis are no longer carrying this alone.
summary: What changed is the plumbing, and it changed for the worse. Credit stopped widening on Tuesday; today it resumed — HY OAS +9bp to 3.72 (1m z=1.14, 97th percentile of the year), CCC +18bp to 14.05 (+520bp YTD), BBB +2bp to 1.22 and IG +1bp to 0.98, both sitting at the 100th percentile. HYG/IEF fell 1.1% with a 1m z of -1.77. Volatility did not ease, it went vertical: VIX +29.6% to 34.15 (z=3.38, acceleration z=1.57), VIX3M +16.4% to 29.64, and VIX/VIX3M at 1.152, the 98th percentile and still accelerating. The credit & vol composite deteriorated to -66 from -50 and the risk regime slipped to -22. This is the acceleration that matters: the sell-off is speeding up, not exhausting.

Equity damage broadened beyond silicon. SPX -2.7% to 7,010 (1m z=-2.32), NDX -4.2%, QQQ/SPY at the 0th percentile. Semis were hit again — SOXX -7.0%, SMH -6.7% (-26.5% on the month, 24% below its 200-day), NVDA -8.1% to 142.79 and -33.9% in a month, MU -10.5%, AMD -9.0%, TSM -6.8%, ASML -6.7%, EWT -6.2%, EWY -5.7%. But today the rest of megacap joined: AMZN -6.0%, GOOGL -4.7% (0.5th percentile), ORCL -8.0%, MSFT -3.2%. MTUM -4.1% with a 1m z of -3.41; SPHB/SPLV -5.3% and -19.0% on the month. The one thing that still works is dispersion: RSP/SPY +1.8% to the 100th percentile (z=3.2), IWM/SPY +1.2%, XHB/SPY +2.5%, KRE/SPY +1.9%, IYT/SPY +1.8%, and IGV/SMH +3.5% on the day, +12.4% on the month. The median stock is still outperforming the index into a 2.7% down day.

The macro tension is unchanged but the hedges finally functioned. Treasuries bid — TLT +1.3%, IEF +0.8% (z=0.9, turning up), LQD +0.5%, 30y -2bp to 5.29 — the first session in weeks where duration paid for equity risk. Underneath, the squeeze is real-rate, not nominal: the 3-month bill is 4.37% (+15bp on the month, 100th percentile) against effective funds at 3.88%, the 10-year real yield is 2.79% with acceleration z=0.69 and 22% above its 200-day, while 5-year breakevens are 2.11% (-37bp on the month, z=-1.76) and 10-year 2.12% — both at the 0th percentile of the year. Gasoline -24.4% and Brent -22.5% on the month, DBC z=-2.93. Yet core CPI is still turning up (+30bp, z=0.93) and the inflation composite reads 61. The market is pricing a demand shock into a front end that still refuses to cut; 3m10y has flattened 23bp in a month to 0.55.

Outside the US the dollar is the transmission mechanism and it is still tightening. DXY +0.2% to 103.99 (96th percentile), USDMXN +2.9% to 19.724 — a fresh 52-week high, 100th percentile — USDKRW +0.5%, CEW -2.7% on the month, AUDUSD -6.3% (z=-2.41), AUDJPY -4.9%. USDBRL is +18.1% on the month with a 1m z of 4.9 even after today's 1.2% retracement. Metals are not a haven in this tape: gold -2.7% to 3,465 (z=-3.09, 0th percentile), silver -5.2% to 38.62, platinum -4.1%, GDX -3.4%, gold/silver 89.73 at the 100th percentile — that is collateral being sold, not fear being bought. Crypto keeps making lower lows: BTC 58,259 (-27.2% on the month), MSTR -8.3% and -49.1%, COIN -5.4%. The green on the screen is narrow and defensive: XLP, XLU, XLRE, SPLV, KIE, LMT +1.2%, DE +3.4%, HD +0.8%, MCD +0.7%, CVX +0.9%, ITB +0.4%, and natural gas +10.0% to 3.655, +40.5% on the month. Own that list, hedge the rest.

good.text: Breadth refuses to break: RSP/SPY +1.8% to the 100th percentile (1m z=3.2), IWM/SPY +1.2%, KRE/SPY +1.9%, XHB/SPY +2.5%, IYT/SPY +1.8%, XRT/SPY +1.3%. The median stock is still beating the index inside a 2.7% index decline — this is a de-rating of crowded exposure, not a broad liquidation.

Treasuries finally hedged equities: TLT +1.3%, IEF +0.8% (z=0.9, turning up), LQD +0.5%, 30y -2bp to 5.29. After weeks of stocks and bonds falling together, duration paid on a down day — the single most important change versus yesterday.

Inflation expectations are capitulating, giving the Fed cover: 5y breakevens 2.11% (-37bp on the month, 1m z=-1.76) and 10y 2.12%, both the 0th percentile of the year, with gasoline -24.4% and Brent -22.5% over the same month.

The defensive and consumer-staple complex keeps absorbing the flows: XLP +0.3% (rel. strength +14.6% 1m), XLU +0.3%, SPLV +0.3%, KIE +0.5%, HD +0.8%, MCD +0.7%, DE +3.4%, LMT +1.2%. A real destination exists for money leaving AI.
India is the one equity market in an uptrend: Sensex +1.8% today, INDA +13.5% on the month with a 1m z of 3.03 and acceleration z=2.54, relative strength +24.1% vs the S&P.

The labor data is not confirming the market's growth scare: initial claims 189k (-14.9% y/y, 0th percentile), continuing claims 1.697m (-12.9% y/y), unemployment 4.1% and falling, JOLTS openings +4.6%.

bad.text: Volatility is accelerating, not peaking: VIX +29.6% to 34.15 (1m z=3.38, acceleration z=1.57), VIX3M +16.4% to 29.64, and the VIX/VIX3M term structure at 1.152 — 98th percentile and still turning up. SKEW -0.9% to 139 says the hedging is happening at-the-money now, not in the tails.

Credit's one-day truce reversed: HY OAS +9bp to 3.72, CCC +18bp to 14.05, BBB +2bp to 1.22, IG +1bp to 0.98 — the latter three at the 100th percentile of the year. HYG/IEF -1.1% with a 1m z of -1.77. The credit & vol composite fell to -66 from -50.

The semis bear market deepened and spread: SOXX -7.0%, SMH -6.7% (-26.5% 1m, 24% below 200-day), NVDA -8.1% to 142.79, MU -10.5%, AMD -9.0%, TSM -6.8%, ASML -6.7%, EWT -6.2%, EWY -5.7%. And this time megacap followed: AMZN -6.0%, GOOGL -4.7%, ORCL -8.0%.

Real rates are tightening into a growth scare: 10y TIPS 2.79% with acceleration z=0.69 and 22% above its 200-day, 3-month bill 4.37% at the 100th percentile versus 3.88% effective funds, while breakevens sit at the 0th percentile. The rates composite is -48.

The dollar is squeezing EM funding harder: USDMXN +2.9% to 19.724, a fresh 52-week high and 100th percentile; USDBRL +18.1% on the month (1m z=4.9); CEW -2.7%; AUDUSD -6.3% (z=-2.41); AUDJPY -4.9%. The dollar composite is -58 and EEM -3.8%.

Hard assets are being sold as collateral, not bought as havens: gold -2.7% to 3,465 (z=-3.09, 0th percentile), silver -5.2%, platinum -4.1%, GDX -3.4%, copper -0.7% (-18.1% 1m), with gold/silver at 89.73, the 100th percentile. Crypto confirms: BTC 58,259, MSTR -8.3%, COIN -5.4%.

trades.name: Software over semis
trades.line: Long IGV / short SMH: software keeps winning the AI unwind
trades.expr: Equal dollar long IGV, short SMH. Size 1x each leg.
trades.thesis: The AI trade is being de-rated through hardware, not code. Capex-exposed silicon carries the valuation and the inventory risk; software's revenue is subscription and its multiple already compressed (IGV -12.9% YTD vs SMH +10.5%). The ratio has moved 12.4% in a month and the drivers — collapsing semi pricing power, Taiwan/Korea de-rating — are intact.
trades.trigger: IGV/SMH +3.5% today and +25.5% over 3 months, 1m z=1.78. SMH -6.7% with SOXX -7.0%, MU -10.5%, AMD -9.0%, NVDA -8.1%; SMH relative strength -19.6% on the month versus IGV -9.7%.
trades.stop: A single-day reversal in which SMH outperforms IGV by more than 5% cumulatively, or NVDA reclaiming its 200-day (currently 29% above spot).
trades.target: Another 8% on the ratio, roughly the pace of the last four weeks.

trades.name: Staples over discretionary
trades.line: Long XLP / short XLY: pay for the defensive bid
trades.expr: Long XLP, short XLY, equal dollars. This is effectively short AMZN/TSLA against the staples cash-flow complex.
trades.thesis: With UMich sentiment at 48 and the equity drawdown now hitting the wealth effect, the consumer trade is bifurcating: value retail (WMT, COST, TGT, HD) and staples work, aspirational discretionary does not. XLY/XLP is at the 0th percentile of the year and still falling.
trades.trigger: XLY -2.7% versus XLP +0.3% today; XLY/XLP -3.0% on the day and -8.8% over three months. XLP relative strength +14.6% 1m, XLP at the 97th percentile of its 52-week range. AMZN -6.0%, TSLA -5.4%.
trades.stop: XLY/XLP reclaiming its 200-day (ratio 8.9% below it) or a 4% adverse move on the pair.

trades.name: Credit decompression
trades.line: Short HYG vs long IEF: credit decompression resumed
trades.expr: Short HYG against a long in IEF, equal dollars — the cash version of buying HY protection. Funded carry is negative but the convexity is the point.
trades.thesis: Yesterday's one-day spread tightening was a bounce, not a turn. HY OAS has widened 102bp in three months and CCCs 366bp while IG and BBB sit at 100th-percentile spreads for the year. With VIX 34 and equity vol accelerating, HY has not repriced the equity drawdown yet — HYG is only -3.2% over three months.
trades.trigger: HY OAS +9bp to 3.72 today, CCC +18bp to 14.05, BBB +2bp, IG +1bp, after one session of tightening. HYG/IEF -1.1% with a 1m z of -1.77 and rolling over; IEF turning up (z=0.9) as Treasuries finally hedge.
trades.stop: HY OAS back below 3.40 (a 30bp+ tightening) or 2.5% loss on the combined position.
trades.target: 4% on the pair, consistent with HY OAS pushing toward 4.25% while the belly rallies.

trades.name: Long USD vs peso
trades.line: Long USDMXN: EM funding squeeze at 52-week highs
trades.expr: Long USDMXN spot/forward, or short EWW as the equity proxy. Keep the peso leg small — carry is against you.
trades.thesis: The dollar composite at -58 is the real tightening channel. The peso is the highest-carry, most crowded long in EM and is breaking first; USDBRL already moved 18.1% in a month with a 1m z of 4.9. Positioning unwinds in high-carry crosses do not stop at the first 52-week high.
trades.trigger: USDMXN +2.9% today to 19.724 — a fresh 52-week high, 100th percentile, +16.4% over three months, 1m z=1.95. CEW -1.5% on the week, EEM -3.8%, USDKRW +0.5%, AUDUSD -6.3% on the month.
trades.stop: USDMXN back below 19.00, or DXY breaking under its 200-day (currently 3.9% below spot).

trades.name: Long natural gas
trades.line: Long natgas: the only bid left in commodities
trades.expr: Long front-month natural gas futures, or the UNG/first-nearby equivalent. Size for 10% daily ranges.
trades.thesis: Every other commodity is in liquidation — DBC 1m z=-2.93, Brent -22.5%, copper -18.1%, gold -14.2% — yet gas is up 40.5% on the month on weather and power demand. It is the one commodity whose driver is physical, not macro-financial, which makes it the cleanest non-correlated long in a de-risking tape, and it still sits only in the 23rd percentile of its 52-week range.
trades.trigger: NATGAS +10.0% today to 3.655, +8.4% on the week, 1m z=2.05 with acceleration z=2.18, turning up and 23% above its 200-day — the only green commodity print on the board.
trades.stop: A close back below 3.20 (roughly -12%), which would mean the weather bid has failed.

trades.name: India over EM
trades.line: Long INDA / short EEM: India is the one EM working
trades.expr: Long INDA, short EEM, equal dollars. This isolates India against the Korea/Taiwan/China/Brazil complex that dominates the EEM index.
trades.thesis: EM is not one asset. The EM index is a semis-and-commodity index: Taiwan, Korea and China are the drawdown and USDBRL/USDMXN are the funding stress. India is domestic demand with a currency that is actually strengthening — USDINR -2.9% on the month, 1m z=-2.76, the only major EM currency rallying against the dollar.
trades.trigger: Sensex +1.8% today against EEM -3.8%; INDA +13.5% on the month with 1m z=3.03 and acceleration z=2.54, relative strength +24.1% vs the S&P, while EEM/SPY sits at the 0th percentile and EWT -6.2%, EWY -5.7%.
trades.stop: INDA/EEM giving back 5%, or USDINR turning back above 94.

trades.name: Short the levered bitcoin proxy
trades.line: Short MSTR: levered bitcoin proxy still in free fall
trades.expr: Short MSTR outright, or buy puts 3 months out. Keep size modest — borrow is expensive and squeezes are violent.
trades.thesis: MSTR is a levered, premium-to-NAV claim on bitcoin at a moment when bitcoin itself is making lower lows and the whole balance-sheet-crypto model is being repriced. The premium compresses faster than BTC falls: MSTR -49.1% on the month against BTC -27.2%.
trades.trigger: MSTR -8.3% today to 71.14, -21.2% on the week, 46% below its 200-day, 0th percentile of its 52-week range; BTC -2.5% to 58,259 and IBIT 1m z=-1.98; COIN -5.4% and -39.4% on the month.
trades.stop: MSTR closing above 88 (+24%), or BTC reclaiming 66,000.
